PullRequest.Title: nes: serve documents of every scheme except a denylist
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #337933

## Problem

With inline completions unification on, next edit suggestions (NES) register for every document and exclude the separate completions provider. However, NES only tracked `file`, `untitled` and notebook documents, so any other document got no inline suggestions at all. For example, documents from an extension's `FileSystemProvider` (Zowe Explorer, InterSystems ObjectScript, memfs) were affected. Turning unification off was the only workaround.

## Change

- **Denylist instead of allowlist** in `documentFilter.ts`. NES now tracks every document except:
  - the schemes ghost text already ignores: `output`, `search-editor`, `comment`, `git`, chat editing snapshots;
  - chat-internal models that users don't type in: chat code blocks, chat input, chat terminal output, chat editing original models. Their content changes would otherwise show up as recent edits in other documents' prompts.

  Language enablement and content exclusion checks are unchanged.
- **Files that commonly hold secrets are never context for other documents** (`sensitiveFiles.ts`): `.env`, `.env.*`, `mcp.json`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `.netrc`, `.git-credentials`, `.pgpass`, SSH private keys, and `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`.
  - NES still serves these files while you edit them.
  - Their edits and content are left out of requests for other documents. This covers normal and speculative requests, and neighbor file snippets.
  - This also applies to such `file:` documents, which were previously sent as context.

There are no changes to provider registration or core.

## How to test

1. Install an extension that contributes a `FileSystemProvider`, such as the repro from the issue, and open one of its documents.
2. Set `"github.copilot.chat.advanced.inlineEdits.unification": true`.
3. Type in a function body. An inline suggestion appears, and Tab accepts it.

Video of the repro from the issue (`repro-bug:` file system, unification on): [nes-virtual-fs.mp4](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/blob/main/vscode/issue-337933/nes-virtual-fs.mp4)

## Validation

- `cd extensions/copilot && npx vitest --run --pool=forks src/extension/inlineEdits/test/vscode-node/documentFilter.spec.ts src/extension/inlineEdits/test/node/nextEditProviderContext.spec.ts src/extension/inlineEdits/test/node/nextEditProviderCaching.spec.ts src/extension/inlineEdits/test/node/nextEditProviderSpeculative.spec.ts src/extension/inlineEdits/test/node/nesXtabHistoryTracker.spec.ts`: **passed** (5 files; 79 passed, 2 skipped).
  - The two new tests **fail** with the source changes reverted: the scheme table in `documentFilter.spec.ts`, and `.env` exclusion in the new `nextEditProviderContext.spec.ts`.
- `cd extensions/copilot && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`: **passed**.
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`: **passed**, no findings.
- `cd extensions/copilot && npx vitest --run --pool=forks src/extension/inlineEdits src/extension/xtab src/platform/inlineEdits`: 2571 passed. 11 tests **failed**, all in `ignoreImportChanges.spec.ts` and `xtabProvider.spec.ts`. They fail the same way without this change, because the built diff worker file they need is missing in a fresh worktree.
- Running Code OSS with the issue's `FileSystemProvider` repro and unification on:
  - the `repro-bug:` document gets NES suggestions, and the trace log shows NES served them;
  - user `settings.json` and `.env` are served too;
  - the request sent for a `file:` document includes `settings.json` and the virtual document as context, but no `.env` content.

## Not in this PR

- Prompt paths drop the URI scheme. If a virtual file system is mounted as a workspace folder at `/`, a cross-file edit can target the wrong URI.
- `.copilotignore` files in non-`file` workspace folders are not discovered. This affects ghost text too.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed admission condition, VSCodeWorkspace-to-InlineEditTriggerer call path, absence of close cleanup, and TextDocument-to-MirrorTextModel retention are all directly visible in repository code. Exact session file counts and document sizes vary, affecting severity but not the retention mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Closed virtual-file TextDocument objects and their full line arrays
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained memory grows with the cumulative bytes of every distinct non-file document edited during the extension-host lifetime, even after those documents are closed.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded extension-host memory growth and increasing GC pressure during long virtual-filesystem editing sessions.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous allowlist rejected non-file/non-untitled virtual documents before they entered VSCodeWorkspace, so edits to zowe-ds:, memfs:, and other FileSystemProvider documents could not populate InlineEditTriggerer's per-document state.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The denylist now admits every unlisted scheme. Each edit to one of those newly tracked documents reaches InlineEditTriggerer, which stores LastChange(e.document) in docToLastChangeMap; that map has no document-close cleanup and lives until the feature is disposed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 46 replaces the old file/untitled/notebook allowlist with a check that rejects only `ignoredSchemes`, newly allowing arbitrary FileSystemProvider schemes to reach the leaking per-document trigger map.
Findings.Title: Dispose trigger state when virtual documents close
Findings.Impact: A user who edits and closes many virtual files or dataset members in one VS Code session retains each closed document's complete text in the Copilot extension host. Large/generated virtual files make memory and GC cost grow throughout the session rather than returning after close.
Findings.Evidence: VSCodeWorkspace creates a DocumentId for every document admitted by this condition and InlineEditTriggerer._registerDocumentChangeListener stores `new LastChange(e.document)` keyed by that id. InlineEditTriggerer registers only change and selection listeners, not onDidCloseTextDocument, so entries are removed only during rejection cooldown or feature disposal. VS Code's ExtHostDocumentData.document object closes over ExtHostDocumentData, whose MirrorTextModel `_lines` remain readable after dispose, proving the retained TextDocument keeps full text alive.
Findings.Recommendation: Register document-close cleanup (or observe removals from VSCodeWorkspace.openDocuments) and call `docToLastChangeMap.deleteAndDispose` for the closed DocumentId. Keep the broader scheme support; bound trigger state to currently open documents.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit and close documents provided by a virtual FileSystemProvider (for example zowe-ds: or memfs:) with NES unification enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The document must pass DocumentFilter/isCopilotIgnored before VSCodeWorkspace exposes it; an automatic inline-completion opportunity then checks the NES cache and, on a miss, waits for stateless model inference before a suggestion can appear. Per-document trigger state remains after close, although that retention is not required for progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan file workspaces for .copilotignore and, when regex exclusions require it, read up to 1 KiB of content
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Shared initialization scan once per service attempt; content reads only when regex rules exist and no cached verdict is usable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old scheme allowlist returned false before invoking isCopilotIgnored for these virtual documents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial eligibility decision must finish before the newly admitted virtual document is tracked; subsequent settled verdicts are cached.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Coalesced per repository/non-git key, batched up to ten repositories and limited to five concurrent batches; reused for the rule TTL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Non-file virtual documents were rejected by the scheme gate and did not reach this policy lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold eligibility check waits for the relevant coalesced rule fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send a stateless next-edit inference request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one new request per uncached current document state/opportunity after existing pending/speculative reuse; rapid edits may cancel or supersede stale requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These virtual documents were not tracked, so NES issued no inference request for them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On a cache miss, inference is the main suggestion-latency boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Request work scales with edit opportunities and cache misses; retained memory scales with the cumulative text bytes of distinct virtual documents edited and closed over the extension-host lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Eligibility checks may overlap while initial policy resolution is pending; workspace ignore initialization is shared, content-exclusion rule fetches are coalesced and limited to five batches, and file reads are limited to ten. NES joins matching in-flight/speculative requests and cancels or supersedes stale work according to the existing request manager.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Content-exclusion verdicts are cached per URI after rules/repository state settle, with rule TTL invalidation; rule fetches coalesce. NES uses its existing edit cache and pending-request reuse. The trigger-state DisposableMap has no close-time eviction, which is the reportable issue.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new scheme admission, trigger-map insertion, lack of close cleanup, and retained MirrorTextModel line storage are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number and size of virtual documents edited per session varies by extension and workflow; long-lived dataset/remote-explorer sessions can accumulate many, while short sessions may see little growth.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable memory regression: the feature expansion is valid, but newly tracked virtual documents expose a pre-existing trigger-map lifecycle gap and retain full closed document contents without a bound.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build regular and speculative NES requests while sensitive files are among recent documents or edit history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: History is obtained, filtered locally with canUseAsContext, projected/serialized, and then passed to the existing stateless provider. Speculative construction follows the same filtering before its existing remote request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send regular or speculative stateless next-edit request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing one-per-new-state behavior after cache/pending reuse; filtering does not add requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request boundary ran with unfiltered history and potentially larger payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing inference remains on the regular suggestion path and speculative work remains reusable/off the immediate path when created speculatively.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Project bounded document/edit history into the request payload
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded projection per request construction; sensitive entries are now removed first.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All bounded history entries were projected, including sensitive files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Regular construction is before inference; speculative construction occurs before the speculative send.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Filtering scans at most the bounded recent-document/history collections (history trackers cap at 50 entries and rejected edits at 3); serialized/network bytes decrease when sensitive entries are removed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Regular matching requests join existing pending work; speculative requests use the single pending/claimed manager behavior already present. The new filtering itself is synchronous and per request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: NES edit and speculative caches are unchanged. Sensitive-name classification is recomputed per bounded entry and needs no lifecycle cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both regular and speculative call sites use the new bounded filters before projection/request dispatch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual payload reduction depends on whether sensitive files appear in the bounded recent history.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the added local scans are bounded and reduce downstream serialization/network payload when they match.

Scenarios.Scenario: Append neighbor-file snippets while constructing an NES prompt
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The already-computed neighbor list is scanned synchronously; sensitive URIs and duplicate documents are skipped before token counting, then the existing model request consumes the resulting prompt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Format selected snippets into prompt text
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one formatting operation per selected, deduplicated snippet within the token budget.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Sensitive neighbor snippets were token-counted, formatted, and included when budget allowed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the existing inference request; the changed check can only skip work and bytes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the completed NES prompt to the existing model provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged request cardinality; only prompt contents can shrink.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundary sent prompts that could include those neighbor snippets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing model boundary remains on cache-miss suggestion latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One local pass over the supplied neighbor snippets; effective included cardinality is further bounded by token budget and document deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial synchronous prompt construction; no new parallel work or boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced. DocumentId interning already exists; sensitive classification is a small basename/extension set lookup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added predicate executes before token counting and selection, with no changed upstream retrieval.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Neighbor-list size and the frequency of sensitive matches vary, but the changed operation cannot increase selected snippets or payload size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the change removes local tokenization/formatting and outbound bytes for matching snippets without adding a boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and traced document admission, history filtering, prompt construction, policy checks, and model-request paths. Submitted one medium-confidence/high-mechanism-confidence unbounded-retention finding for closed virtual documents held by InlineEditTriggerer; no other changed mechanism met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
